## Measured 2026-07-31 at HEAD

Two subcommands of `pm graph`, run back to back against the same workspace and reporting the same cache fingerprint `d9ffaeb9eaa5`, disagree about how large the graph is:

- `pm graph analyze --json` -> `edge_count: 10046`
- `pm graph centrality --json` -> `edge_count: 7351`

Same field name, same command, same node_count of 2222, same fingerprint, 26.8 percent apart. Nothing in either envelope names the convention it used.

## Root cause

`src/sdk/graph/run.ts:834` emits `graph.edges().length` — the directed count of stored edges.
`src/sdk/graph/centrality.ts:273` emits `edgeCount: degreeSum / 2` — an undirected count derived by halving the adjacency degree sum.

Both values are individually correct for their own analytic. Neither is labelled. A `directed` flag is already in scope at the centrality call site and is passed to `centralityRow`, but the halving is applied unconditionally, so on a genuinely directed adjacency the reported value is not a count of anything.

## Why this matters beyond cosmetics

`edge_count` is the field an agent uses to decide whether a traversal is affordable and whether a graph enrichment wave changed anything. Two conventions under one name make every cross-subcommand comparison wrong in a way that reads as data loss: an agent that reads centrality after analyze concludes 2,695 edges disappeared. It is also the exact shape of defect the cross-channel-disagreement catalog entry on the relevance engine describes — two channels that should agree about one fact, with no predicate stating which is authoritative.

## The general form

The graph command family has at least three independent edge-counting sites: the two above plus `src/sdk/graph/conformance.ts:74` (fixture-declared) and `src/sdk/dependencies.ts:653` (deduplicated by `source::target::kind` key). The audit profile reports 10046 while a direct read of the stored `dependencies[]` arrays plus parent-field edges totals 10499, so a fourth canonicalization is applied somewhere in the audit path. Four counting conventions, one field name, zero declarations.

## Minimal correct shape

`edge_count` declares its convention in the envelope (`edge_basis: directed | undirected | deduplicated`), or the field is renamed per convention so no two subcommands publish different semantics under one key. Whichever is chosen, a contract test asserts that every subcommand of `pm graph` that emits `edge_count` also emits its basis, and that two subcommands sharing a basis report the same number for the same fingerprint.
Four edge-counting conventions publish under one edge_count field: graph analyze reports 10046 and graph centrality 7351 for the same graph at the same cache fingerprint
pm graph subcommands emit directed, undirected, deduplicated, and fixture edge counts under one undeclared field name, so cross-subcommand comparison reports phantom edge loss.

Every graph subcommand emitting edge_count also emits the basis that produced it; A contract test asserts basis presence and cross-subcommand agreement within a basis for one cache fingerprint; The unconditional degreeSum/2 halving is either justified by an asserted undirected adjacency or made conditional on the directed flag already in scope; graph audit profile totals reconcile against a directly derived stored-edge count, or the canonicalization it applies is declared
Makes graph size a trustworthy measurement so enrichment waves can be verified rather than believed.
The tracker is entering a deliberate graph enrichment programme; edge_count is the before/after measure and it currently has four meanings.
Every pm graph subcommand that emits edge_count declares the counting convention it used, and two subcommands sharing a convention agree for one fingerprint.
analyze emits 10046 (directed stored edges), centrality emits 7351 (degreeSum/2, undirected), audit profile emits 10046 against 10499 raw stored edges; no envelope names its basis.
